text: A jar has 18 beads. You remove 7. How many remain?
label: C
hints: Name the starting quantity and describe what changes.
Sketch the quantities before and after the change.
Check whether your result should be larger or smaller than the starting amount.
solution: Removing means subtraction: 18 − 7 = 11.

text: A basket has 9 green balls and 6 yellow balls. How many balls are there?
label: D
hints: Name the starting quantity and describe what changes.
Sketch the quantities before and after the change.
Check whether your result should be larger or smaller than the starting amount.
solution: Add the two groups: 9 + 6 = 15.

text: A rope is 24 cm long. A 9 cm piece is cut off. How long is the remaining rope?
label: E
hints: Name the starting quantity and describe what changes.
Sketch the quantities before and after the change.
Check whether your result should be larger or smaller than the starting amount.
solution: Subtract the removed length: 24 − 9 = 15 cm.

text: There are 4 boxes with 6 pencils in each. How many pencils?
label: A
hints: Find the equal groups in the problem.
Write the number of groups and the size of each group separately.
Use repeated addition to check your multiplication.
solution: Four equal groups of six give 4 × 6 = 24.

text: A tray holds 5 rows of 3 muffins. How many muffins?
label: B
hints: Find the equal groups in the problem.
Write the number of groups and the size of each group separately.
Use repeated addition to check your multiplication.
solution: Five rows of three give 5 × 3 = 15.

text: Seven bags each hold 2 marbles. How many marbles in total?
label: C
hints: Find the equal groups in the problem.
Write the number of groups and the size of each group separately.
Use repeated addition to check your multiplication.
solution: Seven equal groups of two give 7 × 2 = 14.

text: Twenty-four counters are shared equally among 6 children. How many does each get?
label: D
hints: Identify the total and what must be equal.
Draw equal groups and share the total between them.
Multiply your proposed result by the divisor to check the total.

text: How many groups of 5 can you make from 35 buttons?
label: E
hints: Identify the total and what must be equal.
Draw equal groups and share the total between them.
Multiply your proposed result by the divisor to check the total.

text: Eighteen flowers go equally into 3 vases. How many flowers per vase?
label: A
hints: Identify the total and what must be equal.
Draw equal groups and share the total between them.
Multiply your proposed result by the divisor to check the total.

text: What is 5 + 2 × 6?
label: B
hints: Look for brackets and multiplication before calculating.
Evaluate one high-priority operation and rewrite the expression.
Check that every operation was used exactly once.
solution: Multiply first: 2 × 6 = 12, then 5 + 12 = 17.

text: What is (4 + 3) × 2?
label: C
hints: Look for brackets and multiplication before calculating.
Evaluate one high-priority operation and rewrite the expression.
Check that every operation was used exactly once.
solution: Evaluate the brackets first: 4 + 3 = 7, then 7 × 2 = 14.

text: What is 20 − 3 × 4?
label: D
hints: Look for brackets and multiplication before calculating.
Evaluate one high-priority operation and rewrite the expression.
Check that every operation was used exactly once.
solution: Multiply first: 3 × 4 = 12, then 20 − 12 = 8.

text: Choose one of 2 hats and one of 3 scarves. How many different hat-and-scarf outfits?
label: E
hints: Choose one feature to keep fixed while you list cases.
Use a table or small tree to organise the possibilities.
Check that every listed case satisfies the rules and appears only once.
solution: Each hat pairs with three scarves: 3 + 3 = 6.

text: How many different two-digit numbers can use 1, 2 and 3 without repeating a digit?
label: A
hints: Choose one feature to keep fixed while you list cases.
Use a table or small tree to organise the possibilities.
Check that every listed case satisfies the rules and appears only once.
solution: List 12, 13, 21, 23, 31, 32: six numbers.

text: A menu has 3 soups and 2 breads. Choose one of each. How many different meals?
label: B
hints: Choose one feature to keep fixed while you list cases.
Use a table or small tree to organise the possibilities.
Check that every listed case satisfies the rules and appears only once.
solution: Each of the three soups pairs with two breads, making six meals.

text: A whole number is even, greater than 5 and less than 9. Which option fits all three rules?
label: C
hints: Rewrite each condition as a separate check.
Try a small candidate and test it against every condition.
Cross out a candidate only when you can name the condition it breaks.
solution: Of the options, only 6 is even and strictly between 5 and 9.

text: A code digit is odd and greater than 6. It is not 9. Which digit is it?
label: D
hints: Rewrite each condition as a separate check.
Try a small candidate and test it against every condition.
Cross out a candidate only when you can name the condition it breaks.
solution: Odd digits above 6 are 7 and 9. Excluding 9 leaves 7.

text: A number is a multiple of 3, greater than 10 and less than 14. Which is it?
label: E
hints: Rewrite each condition as a separate check.
Try a small candidate and test it against every condition.
Cross out a candidate only when you can name the condition it breaks.
solution: 12 is the only multiple of 3 strictly between 10 and 14.

text: An arrow points up. Turn it a quarter-turn clockwise. Which way does it point?
label: A
hints: Choose a distinctive corner, edge or mark to follow.
Keep that feature fixed in your mind as you turn or combine the shapes.
Compare several features, not just the overall outline.
solution: A clockwise quarter-turn moves up to right.

text: You face north and turn left twice, each time a quarter-turn. Which way do you face?
label: B
hints: Choose a distinctive corner, edge or mark to follow.
Keep that feature fixed in your mind as you turn or combine the shapes.
Compare several features, not just the overall outline.
solution: The first left turn faces west; the second faces south.

text: A square has a dot at its top-left corner. Rotate it half a turn. Where is the dot?
label: C
hints: Choose a distinctive corner, edge or mark to follow.
Keep that feature fixed in your mind as you turn or combine the shapes.
Compare several features, not just the overall outline.
solution: A half-turn takes each corner to the opposite corner.

text: A rectangle is 5 cm long and 3 cm wide. What is its perimeter?
label: D
hints: Decide whether the question asks about the boundary or the inside.
Label the known lengths and find one missing length at a time.
Check your units: length uses units and area uses square units.
solution: The boundary is 5 + 3 + 5 + 3 = 16 cm.

text: A square has sides of 4 cm. What is its area?
label: E
hints: Decide whether the question asks about the boundary or the inside.
Label the known lengths and find one missing length at a time.
Check your units: length uses units and area uses square units.
solution: Area is side × side: 4 × 4 = 16 cm².

text: A rectangle covers 18 cm² and is 3 cm wide. How long is it?
label: A
hints: Decide whether the question asks about the boundary or the inside.
Label the known lengths and find one missing length at a time.
Check your units: length uses units and area uses square units.
solution: Length × 3 = 18, so length = 18 ÷ 3 = 6 cm.

text: What comes next: 3, 6, 9, 12, …?
label: B
hints: Describe what stays the same and what changes.
Look for the shortest repeating block or a consistent difference.
Test your proposed rule on more than one step.
solution: The difference is three each time, so 12 + 3 = 15.

text: A pattern repeats red, blue, blue. What colour is the seventh item?
label: C
hints: Describe what stays the same and what changes.
Look for the shortest repeating block or a consistent difference.
Test your proposed rule on more than one step.
solution: Two blocks contain six items. The seventh starts a new block with red.

text: What comes next: 20, 18, 16, 14, …?
label: D
hints: Describe what stays the same and what changes.
Look for the shortest repeating block or a consistent difference.
Test your proposed rule on more than one step.
solution: Subtract two each time: 14 − 2 = 12.

text: Two identical notebooks cost 6 euros. At the same price each, what do 4 notebooks cost?
label: E
hints: Identify the two quantities that change together.
Compare a single group with the requested number of groups.
Check that the same scale factor connects both quantities.
solution: The number of notebooks doubles, so the cost doubles to 12 euros.

text: A recipe for 3 people uses 2 cups of rice. How many cups for 9 people at the same rate?
label: A
hints: Identify the two quantities that change together.
Compare a single group with the requested number of groups.
Check that the same scale factor connects both quantities.
solution: Nine people is three times as many, so use 3 × 2 = 6 cups.

text: Five identical tickets cost 20 euros. What do 2 tickets cost at the same price each?
label: B
hints: Identify the two quantities that change together.
Compare a single group with the requested number of groups.
Check that the same scale factor connects both quantities.
solution: One ticket costs 20 ÷ 5 = 4 euros. Two cost 8 euros.
